market.hypothesis: The market mid price is the best available estimate (baseline to beat).

longshot.hypothesis: Favorite-longshot bias: cheap contracts are overpriced, so true probabilities are more extreme than prices.

memory.hypothesis: Series memory: a series' own past gap between outcome and price persists, so shifting the price by that gap (shrunk when history is short) beats the price.

nn.hypothesis: A small neural network trained on settled markets (price, spread, time of day, category, series memory) can correct the market price. Starts equal to the market; judged only on data it never trained on.

longshot.rec: no measurable edge after 483 resolved — recommend retiring this hypothesis

memory.rec: not beating the market so far (+0.0033) — wait for 0 more resolved before judging

nn.rec: leaning better than the market (-0.0062) — wait for 0 more resolved

progress.definitions: SUCCESS = Brier better than market (95% interval < 0, n ≥ minResolved) AND simulated picks profitable after fees (95% interval > 0, ≥ minPicks). FAILURE = clearly worse than market, or no edge after retireAfter resolved. Recommendations only; nothing changes without owner approval.

skills.name: kalshi-add-predictor
skills.description: Add a new predictor to test a hypothesis about Kalshi markets.

skills.name: kalshi-check-progress
skills.description: Read-only check of whether the Kalshi prediction agent is moving toward its goal: pulls the latest data, runs progress.mjs and explains goal status, pipeline health and each predictor's status vs the market, with recommendations to approve. Use when asked how the agent is doing, whether it is improving or working, about the scorecard, success/failure, or for a scheduled follow-up check. Not for producing new predictions (use kalshi-run-cycle) or changing the strategy (proposals only; owner approves).

skills.name: kalshi-history
skills.description: Gather and use Kalshi history: run the backtest agent on past settled markets, look up what memory knows about a series, import and score the owner's own Kalshi trades from a CSV export, and query the agent's data through the read-only MCP server. Use when asked about past markets or past bets, backtesting, what we know about a series, the owner's trade history, or to set up/use the MCP tools. Not for live predictions (use kalshi-run-cycle), judging the live record (use kalshi-check-progress) or pipeline errors (use kalshi-ops-status).

skills.name: kalshi-live-agent
skills.description: The hourly dev agent for the Kalshi research agent: keeps live mode running (starts the next hour of 10-minute pipeline cycles), checks every pipeline hand-off, fixes clear breakage safely, and writes a short plain-English briefing. Use when a scheduled task or the dashboard's 'Run dev agent now' button asks for the live check, or the owner asks to run the dev agent. Not for one-off local runs (use kalshi-run-cycle), deep diagnosis (use kalshi-ops-status) or strategy changes (owner approves).

skills.name: kalshi-ops-status
skills.description: Check whether the Kalshi agent's machinery is working: recent GitHub Actions runs and deploys (merges to main), whether the 10-minute schedule fires, data freshness, failed steps and their logs, then diagnose and decide whether a human is needed. Use when asked to look at errors, check the status of the recent deploy or runs, why data stopped updating, or before/after merging a change. Not for judging prediction quality (use kalshi-check-progress) or running the pipeline now (use kalshi-run-cycle).

skills.name: kalshi-run-cycle
skills.description: Run one Kalshi research cycle on this machine right now (tests, log predictions, check outcomes, score, progress) and report counts and errors. Use when asked to run, refresh or test the prediction agent/pipeline now, or after changing predict/resolve/score code. Not for repeating on a schedule (the GitHub Action does that every 10 min; to trigger it in the cloud use gh workflow run) and not for judging results (use kalshi-check-progress).

skills.name: save-as-skill
skills.description: This project's convention for saving a script Claude wrote and tested as a reusable skill in .claude/skills/<name>/ (YAML front matter with what/when/not-for description, register in docs/skills.md and CLAUDE.md). Use when a script in this repo will be reused, or the owner says save this as a skill/tool. Not for general skill design, evals or skills outside this repo (use anthropic-skills:skill-creator).

paper.note: SIMULATION ONLY — paper money, nothing is traded. Replay = past settled markets (supporting evidence; the neural net uses out-of-sample predictions only). Forward = live predictions (the record that counts). Fills assume the quoted price; real fills on thin markets can be worse.
